Missing guarantee: single-fetch/validated-value-identity — the kernel reads the shared field more than once, using one read for bounds/validation and a distinct read for the actual use, with no READ_ONCE-into-local snapshot, so the validated value and the consumed value can differ. Unsafe use/state transition: the second, unvalidated read flows into a security-sensitive sink (skb->csum_start/csum_offset + CHECKSUM_PARTIAL in the seed), whose value is later trusted by checksum/offload code as already validated. Consequence: out-of-bounds memory access (read or write) in the TX/checksum-computation path, i.e., kernel memory disclosure or corruption triggered by a racing userspace writer. Key transferable invariant: for any value fetched from shared/writable memory, the copy that passed validation must be bit-identical to the copy that is used. Seed is demonstration-only, never reportable. BRANCHES: branch1=xsk-umem-rereads — within net/xdp and drivers'' AF_XDP TX-completion/metadata paths, find any UMEM-resident field (descriptors addr/len/options, tx_metadata request fields, flags) that is read twice or consumed without a single cached read (validate-then-use on shared memory in the same subsystem but different fields/paths than the seed); branch2=uapi-double-fetch — syscall/ioctl/setsockopt/netlink handler paths where the same user memory location (length, count, pointer, union member) is fetched twice via get_user/copy_from_user/peek so validation and use can diverge under a racing writer; branch3=vm-shared-desc-rereads — virtio/vhost/vdpa/paravirt paths where guest- or device-writable descriptor tables, config space, or packet headers are read multiple times (once checked, once used) or trusted across re-reads without snapshotting; branch4=csum-partial-consumer-trust — sinks of skb->csum_start/skb->csum_offset/CHECKSUM_PARTIAL (software checksum helpers, tunnel/encapsulation copy paths, forwarding) that perform memory access or field arithmetic on those values without re-validating them against skb headroom/length, turning any inconsistently-validated producer into an OOB access.'

{
  "hexsha": "22ba97ea9cc1f63a0d0244fae38057ed452b6ac7",
  "one_line_summary": "xsk: cache csum_start/csum_offset to fix TOCTOU in xsk_skb_metadata()",
  "vulnerability_summary": "Userspace-mapped XSK TX metadata fields csum_start/csum_offset are read twice in xsk_skb_metadata(): once for bounds validation, once for skb assignment. Concurrent writes between reads bypass validation, causing out-of-bounds access during checksum computation.",
  "vulnerability_pattern": "TOCTOU on shared memory: values read from user-writable memory for validation are re-read for use, allowing validation bypass via concurrent modification.",
  "patch": "commit 22ba97ea9cc1f63a0d0244fae38057ed452b6ac7
Author: Jason Xing <kerneljasonxing@gmail.com>
Date:   Sat May 30 12:26:30 2026 +0800

    xsk: cache csum_start/csum_offset to fix TOCTOU in xsk_skb_metadata()
    
    The TX metadata area resides in the UMEM buffer which is memory-mapped
    and concurrently writable by userspace. In xsk_skb_metadata(),
    csum_start and csum_offset are read from shared memory for bounds
    validation, then read again for skb assignment. A malicious userspace
    application can race to overwrite these values between the two reads,
    bypassing the bounds check and causing out-of-bounds memory access
    during checksum computation in the transmit path.
    
    Fix this by reading csum_start and csum_offset into local variables
    once, then using the local copies for both validation and assignment.
    
    Note that other metadata fields (flags, launch_time) and the cached
    csum fields may be mutually inconsistent due to concurrent userspace
    writes, but this is benign: the only security-critical invariant is
    that each field's validated value is the same one used, which local
    caching guarantees.
    
    Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260503200927.73EA1C2BCB4@smtp.kernel.org/
    Reviewed-by: Maciej Fijalkowski <maciej.fijalkowski@intel.com>
    Signed-off-by: Jason Xing <kernelxing@tencent.com>
    Acked-by: Stanislav Fomichev <sdf@fomichev.me>
    Fixes: 48eb03dd2630 ("xsk: Add TX timestamp and TX checksum offload support")
    Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260530042630.80626-1-kerneljasonxing@gmail.com

Author: Jason Xing <kerneljasonxing@gmail.com>
Date:   Sat May 30 12:26:30 2026 +0800

    xsk: cache csum_start/csum_offset to fix TOCTOU in xsk_skb_metadata()
    
    The TX metadata area resides in the UMEM buffer which is memory-mapped
    and concurrently writable by userspace. In xsk_skb_metadata(),
    csum_start and csum_offset are read from shared memory for bounds
    validation, then read again for skb assignment. A malicious userspace
    application can race to overwrite these values between the two reads,
    bypassing the bounds check and causing out-of-bounds memory access
    during checksum computation in the transmit path.
    
    Fix this by reading csum_start and csum_offset into local variables
    once, then using the local copies for both validation and assignment.
    
    Note that other metadata fields (flags, launch_time) and the cached
    csum fields may be mutually inconsistent due to concurrent userspace
    writes, but this is benign: the only security-critical invariant is
    that each field's validated value is the same one used, which local
    caching guarantees.
